newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: World group slams Israel's East Jerusalem plan.
newsitem.headline: World group slams Israel's East Jerusalem plan.

text.p: A global parliamentary group on Monday denounced Israel over its plans to build a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
The Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) adopted a resolution at the end of a meeting in Seoul, criticising the plans as "illegal" and a "major obstacle to peace".
It also deplored "the increasing recourse to violence since the dangerous stalling of the peace process".
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's rightwing government sent bulldozers last month to break ground for homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem.
The move angered Arab neighbours and Palestinian peace partners, sparking raging violence on the West Bank.

"A great responsibility for the stalling of the peace process is in the hands of the Israeli government," Miguel Martinez, chairman of the IPU conference's political committee, told a news conference winding up the meeting.
Netanyahu has opposed Israel's landmark 1993 accord with the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO).
The IPU also supported four-nation peace talks aimed at securing a permanent peace on the Korean peninsula to replace a truce that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
North Korea has agreed to formally respond to the talks, proposed by Washington and Seoul last year, on Wednesday. The talks also include China.
South Korea's National Assembly speaker Kim Soo-han said he regretted that North Korea did not attend the Seoul meeting.
South Korean deputies went to Pyongyang for an IPU conference six years ago.
Almost 600 deputies from 117 countries attended the five-day conference in Seoul. The next IPU conference is due to be held in Cairo, Egypt, in September.
